account: SLB (formerly Schlumberger), including SLB Digital (Delfi, Lumi, Tela, Petrel/Techlog, Ocean)

snapshot.fact: FY2025 revenue was $35.7B, down 2% YoY (down 6% excluding ChampionX's ~$1.5B contribution). SLB operates in more than 100 countries with about 109,000 employees.

Four divisions: Digital ($2.66B in FY2025), Reservoir Performance ($6.82B), Well Construction ($11.86B) and Production Systems ($13.33B). 'All Other' ($1.99B) covers Asset Performance Solutions, Data Center Solutions and SLB Capturi. Operations are organized into 5 Basins and GeoUnits.
Digital revenue grew 9% in 2025, driven by Digital Operations and Platforms & Applications.
Q2 2026 revenue was $8.97B (+5% YoY; -5% YoY excluding ChampionX). Digital was $697M (+18% YoY) with a 28% pretax margin. Digital ARR was $1.04B (+15% YoY). Production Systems was $3.77B (+29% YoY).

Data Center Solutions revenue was $186M in Q2 2026 (+80% YoY). SLB targets a run rate above $1B by YE2026 and above $2B exiting 2027. It also announced an alliance with Liberty Energy for data center power and modular infrastructure.
At the June 2026 Digital Investor Day, CEO Olivier Le Peuch told investors that SLB is 'becoming a digital-first company'.

2030 Digital targets: roughly double Digital revenue/ARR to about $2B, Digital adjusted EBITDA of $1.8-2B and a 38-42% EBITDA margin. Operational adoption targets: autonomous drilling from ~3% to 25%, connected ESPs from ~35% to 60%, formation-evaluation digital add-ons from ~14% to 60%.
Digital TAM is estimated at $25B (2025), rising to $35B, with upside to $50B if AI adoption accelerates. Oil and gas digital spend is 4-5% of industry spend, which SLB calls underpenetrated.
Q3 2026 results will be released on October 23, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. ET, with the call at 9:30 a.m. ET.

tech_posture.fact: Lumi is SLB's data and AI platform. Tela, an agentic AI assistant launched in November 2025, is powered by Lumi and uses LLMs plus domain foundation models. Lumi's agentic framework lets customers build their own Tela agents.
SLB says it has more than 150 AI-enabled applications deployed across its technologies, covering drilling risk prediction, predictive maintenance and production optimization.

Expanded NVIDIA partnership: an 'AI Factory for Energy' reference environment combining NVIDIA Nemotron open models and Omniverse with Delfi and Lumi across ML, generative AI and agentic AI. SLB is also the modular design partner for NVIDIA DSX AI factories.

Launched the SLB digital marketplace with about 200 products from SLB and more than 30 partners, including Delfi/Lumi SaaS, plug-ins, data connectors, and Tela skills, agents and models. Third-party offerings must pass SLB security, interoperability and compatibility certification. Developer portal: developer.slb.com.

At the Investor Day, SLB described an open architecture supporting multi-cloud, on-prem and edge deployment, with hyperscaler partners Microsoft, AWS and Google, plus NVIDIA. It cited 2,600+ experts and more than $3B in R&D since 2016.
AWS expanded its SLB partnership to bring Petrel and Techlog to AWS and to make AWS Energy Data Insights compatible with Lumi (launched at Digital Forum 2024).

Aker BP co-development of an AI-driven platform on Delfi, migrating Aker BP's application portfolio to the cloud. It builds on SLB's OSDU commitment and integration with Microsoft Azure Data Manager for Energy.

Ocean is SLB's software development framework for building plug-ins into Petrel, Studio E&P and Techlog, 'based on state-of-the-art Microsoft technology'. More than 120 Ocean plug-ins exist for Petrel, and there is an Ocean Certified Partner program.

The 10-K says Delfi and Lumi cloud platforms are central to Digital, that Digital Exploration uses high-performance cloud computing, and that Professional Services supports customers' on-prem-to-cloud migrations.

recent_events.fact: Q2 2026 results: completed the acquisition of Tachyus (ML plus physics reservoir modeling; Aqueon platform on more than 7,500 wells), to be integrated into Delfi and Lumi for closed-loop reservoir management.

Definitive agreement to acquire S&P Global Energy's upstream geoscience and petroleum engineering software portfolio, used mainly by US onshore/unconventional operators. Closing is expected 2H26 or early 2027. The tech stack will be integrated gradually, and SLB will co-build AI models on Lumi and Tela with S&P data.
Digital Investor Day set 2030 targets of doubling Digital revenue and EBITDA and positioned SLB as 'digital-first'.
Digital marketplace launched for AI agents, models and apps from SLB and partners.

Q1 2026: Middle East disruption (Qatar force majeure and offshore suspensions, Iraq security) cut revenue about 10.5% sequentially. The CFO said there was no material adjustment to the cost base in the quarter.
Workforce reduction charges totaled about $407M pretax across 2025 ($158M Q1, $66M Q2, $57M Q3, $126M Q4).
ChampionX acquisition closed in Q3 2025 (all-stock, 141M shares, ~$4.9B). Q2 2026 still carried $69M of merger and integration charges.
Launched the Tela agentic AI assistant at ADIPEC, Abu Dhabi.
Expanded the NVIDIA partnership (AI Factory for Energy, DSX modular AI factories).

agent_signals.fact: Ongoing integration of acquired software stacks: ChampionX, Tachyus (into Delfi/Lumi) and the pending S&P Global Energy upstream software portfolio, which SLB will integrate gradually 'keeping existing customer workflows intact'. This creates code migration, consolidation and re-platforming work.

Large desktop/plug-in estate built on Microsoft technology: Petrel, Studio E&P and Techlog extended by Ocean, with more than 120 Petrel plug-ins. This suggests Windows/.NET codebases that must coexist with cloud-native Delfi/Lumi.
Products must support multi-cloud (Microsoft, AWS, Google), on-prem and edge deployment, which multiplies build, test and release targets.

The marketplace requires security, interoperability and compatibility certification for every SLB and third-party listing (about 200 products, 30+ partners). This is a scaled code review and verification burden.
The 10-K discloses phishing and ransomware incidents (not material). The cyber program follows NIST CSF/ISO 27001, with a 3-site 24/7 SOC, and the Cybersecurity Director reports to the CIO.
Margin pressure on Digital: Q1 2026 Digital adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 26.1%, against a 2030 target of 38-42%. Engineering productivity directly affects that margin path.

SLB is itself building agentic AI (Tela, Lumi agentic framework, NVIDIA Nemotron-based AI Factory) and runs developer.slb.com. It is AI-literate, may build internally and may view coding agents through a partner/marketplace lens.
Professional Services supports customers' on-prem-to-cloud migrations, a services line where migration labor could be automated.

pains: HYPOTHESIS: Integrating three acquired codebases (ChampionX digital, Tachyus Aqueon, S&P Global Kingdom/Petra/Harmony-type tools) into Delfi/Lumi without breaking customer workflows strains limited senior engineering capacity.

HYPOTHESIS: Modernizing legacy Windows/.NET desktop apps (Petrel/Techlog/Ocean plug-in API) toward cloud-native Delfi/Lumi is slow and costly, and backward compatibility for 120+ third-party plug-ins makes refactors risky.

HYPOTHESIS: Doubling Digital ARR to ~$2B while lifting EBITDA margin to 38-42% requires shipping more product without growing R&D headcount proportionally, after ~$407M of 2025 workforce reduction charges.
HYPOTHESIS: Marketplace certification (security, interop, compatibility) for ~200 products and growing creates a review/testing bottleneck that coding agents could scale.
HYPOTHESIS: Multi-cloud plus on-prem plus edge deployment targets multiply CI, test and maintenance toil (dependency upgrades, CVE remediation) across the portfolio.
HYPOTHESIS: Internal IT (under the CIO, within the Chief Performance Officer's org) carries ERP/back-office legacy and post-merger system consolidation from ChampionX.

openers: You've committed to doubling Digital to ~$2B with 38-42% EBITDA margins by 2030 while integrating Tachyus and the S&P Global software portfolio. How much of that integration and re-platforming work is sitting on the same engineering teams that need to ship new Lumi/Tela capabilities, and what gets deprioritized?

Petrel, Techlog and the Ocean ecosystem carry a lot of Microsoft/.NET desktop code that has to keep working for 120+ partner plug-ins while you move to cloud-native Delfi/Lumi across three hyperscalers plus on-prem. Where does that modernization stand, and what's the hardest part to test safely?

You now certify every marketplace listing for security and interoperability, and you build agents for customers with Tela. How are you using agents inside your own software engineering org today, and what would you need to see to trust an autonomous agent on a production codebase?

notes: No public CIO, CISO or head-of-software-engineering name was found. The 10-K references a CIO and a Cybersecurity Director without naming them, and the leadership page places IT under Chief Performance Officer Tarek Rizk. Use LinkedIn or Sales Navigator to identify them. Rakesh Jaggi's title appears as 'President, Digital' (2026 releases, leadership page) and as 'President, Digital and Integration' (Tela release Nov 2025, AWS 2024); his bio page metadata is dated 2022. The Digital Investor Day date conflicts: the SLB release and Upstream say June 17, 2026, while the Quartr summary says June 23, 2026, so trust June 17. The 2030 Digital target is described as ~$2B 'revenue' (Reuters via Stockopedia) and as '$2B ARR' (Quartr). Note that FY2025 Digital segment revenue was already $2.66B while ARR is ~$1.04B, so the 'double to $2B' target most likely refers to ARR; verify. The Q1 2026 transcript is internally inconsistent on the full-year Digital EBITDA margin target (35% vs 45%). The Reuters reorg/job-cuts story (new chief performance officer function) is dated Feb 11, 2025, though one aggregator showed a 2026 date. It is older than 12 months. No public evidence was found of a Microsoft EA, GitHub Copilot use, internal AI coding initiatives, IT outsourcing/SI relationships, or software engineering headcount. Q3 2026 results land Oct 23, 2026; refresh after the call. The Ocean 'Microsoft technology' basis is from an undated product page; specific .NET/Windows requirements were not verified (the PDF was blocked by robots.txt).
